PASS -- security review, round 1 of 2 (C34)
PR #264 at f808581187bf33c0513a637304264e9e4029ecb3.

No high-confidence security vulnerability found in the complete 32-file diff.

Trust automation: MenuKey is the closed Up/Down/Enter enum
(crates/core/src/ports.rs:976,988). Tmux executes fixed key arguments without a
shell (crates/tmux/src/lib.rs:338,1094). trust_folder defaults false, and both
CLI and HTTP reject combining it with no_wait
(crates/daemon/src/http/types.rs:192; crates/cli/src/main.rs:363;
crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs:1447). Enter requires the highlighted trust row;
Claude's deny row yields Down, and an absent highlight yields no key
(crates/harnesses/src/trust.rs:100,113). Each loop iteration must recognize the
prompt again. The target is this spawn's allocated pane/requested cwd, not a
separately supplied pane; the displayed folder is not parsed or compared
(crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs:1782). Default refusal sends no key and leaves
the pane and F211 wait live. No new steady-state launch loop: recognition uses
the existing capture; explicit trust automation adds at most one send-keys
per second per outstanding spawn. Live cost measurement belongs to the
performance verdict and was not performed for this security review.

Close-by-ID: runtime posts /v1/close with its caller context, not a boot-roster
target lookup (.omp/extensions/pij/adapters/rust-runtime.ts:817). Authentication,
caller derivation/contradiction checks, and self/recorded-parent/designated-prime
dead-parentless-seat guards remain in the daemon
(crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs:473,791;
crates/daemon/src/http/identity.rs:1411;
crates/daemon/src/http/lifecycle.rs:336,346,506). No PA exception. Held close
coalescing binds action, closer, process identity and pane, and rechecks authority
(crates/daemon/src/http/memory_turn.rs:508,601). Teardown uses only validated,
non-held data.kill_pane, never prose; the daemon retains process ownership and
other-live-holder vetoes (crates/daemon/src/http/lifecycle.rs:319;
.omp/extensions/pij/core/daemon-wire.ts:259;
.omp/extensions/pij/adapters/tmux.ts:175). Ownership is the authorization policy;
process/pane incarnation and shared-holder vetoes are one-directional safety
interlocks (brakes). The pre-existing S220-N003 registry-read residual is not
introduced here and is not re-raised.

Public-content inspection: all five new live fixtures and the full added
test/document content contain no real credential, home path, or account
identifier. No dependency manifest, lockfile, workflow/action, or supply-chain
reference changed. This was manual full-diff inspection, not a secret-scanning
product.

Evidence: independently reran just pr-freeze 264: FINAL at the exact head,
clean detached worktree, all five checks passed, no migration. Independently
verified successful exact-head workflows ci 44483637105 and delivers
44483637164. The delegated security reviewer inspected the complete diff and
downloaded Rust JUnit artifact 14510261401 in memory: trust selection/default
refusal, close caller/parent/prime restrictions, reused panes, and held-close
reparent/revive witnesses passed. Rust summary: 2576 passed, 6 skipped.
Node 22 CI logged 120 passing rust-runtime adapter tests, including inspected
late-child, denied-close and held-close cases; aggregate 2350 passed, 7 skipped.

Proof limits: no local builds/tests, dependency installation/linking, mutation
checks, live trust acceptance, or pane-kill probes. UI behavior is fixture/CI
evidence, not a repeated live session. C33's user-account trust boundary applies.
No new per-seat authentication requirement is asserted.

Harness feedback: the existing dependency-free review-readiness gap recurred.
harness checks has no read-only/no-build evidence mode. Reuse the existing
security role-memory follow-up rather than treating this as a PR defect.
